fullDescription:
Krabi's two inland landmarks with a guide who works in French or German rather than English.

Tiger Cave Temple, Wat Tham Sua, is the harder half. A staircase of 1,260 steps climbs a 309-metre limestone tower to a summit Buddha and a view over the whole province. It takes most people 45 to 60 minutes up, the steps are steep and uneven rather than graded, and the macaques along the route are confident about bags. Early morning or after four in the afternoon is the sane time to do it; the middle of the day on that rock is genuinely punishing.

Huay To waterfall sits inside Khao Phanom Bencha National Park, a series of pools stepping down through rainforest on the flank of Krabi's highest peak. The water is cool and the forest is thick enough that the temperature drops noticeably as you walk in.

The language is the actual product here. Krabi has a great many English-language day tours and very few in French or German, which is why trips like this carry a premium over the English equivalent. If your French or German is stronger than your English, this is the day where the guiding actually reaches you rather than washing past.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off in Krabi, the French or German-speaking guide, Thai lunch, fresh fruit and drinks, and travel insurance.

Seven hours. Temple dress code applies: shoulders and knees covered. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Guide working in French or German, not English
1,260 steps up Tiger Cave Temple's limestone tower
Huay To waterfall in Khao Phanom Bencha forest
Language guiding carries a premium over the English version
Temple dress code: shoulders and knees covered

fullDescription:
An hour at the Krabi night market with someone who can tell you what you are looking at.

Krabi Town's night market runs along the riverfront, and it is a local market with tourists in it rather than a tourist market. Stalls are set up for people buying dinner on the way home, which is why the prices are ordinary and the food turns over fast enough to stay fresh.

An hour is short and that is the honest framing: this is a taste of the market, not a full food tour. What the hour buys you is someone to order for you. Southern Thai food is the spiciest regional cooking in the country and a lot of the best stalls have no English sign and no English menu. Knowing which pot is gaeng tai pla, a fermented fish-gut curry that will take the roof off an unprepared mouth, and which is the mild coconut one, is the difference between a great evening and a ruined one.

Admission fees and tastings are covered, so you are not paying stall by stall.

If you want a full evening of eating, this is not that trip; look for a three-hour food tour instead. If you are in Krabi Town anyway and want an hour that makes the market navigable, it does the job.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, an English-speaking driver, the food tasting, admission fees, drinking water and accident insurance.

One hour at the market plus transfers. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: A working local night market on the Krabi riverfront
An hour, so a taste of the market rather than a food tour
Someone to order for you where there is no English menu
Southern Thai is the spiciest regional cooking in the country
Tastings and admission covered, no paying stall by stall

fullDescription:
Phang Nga Bay on a traditional longtail instead of a speedboat, which changes what you can reach.

Khao Phing Kan is the island; Koh Tapu is the limestone needle offshore that appeared in The Man with the Golden Gun in 1974 and has carried the film's name ever since. Landing at the base of the pinnacle is restricted now because the rock is eroding, so it is viewed from the adjacent beach.

The kayaking is the part a speedboat trip cannot do properly. Phang Nga's limestone is riddled with sea caves and hongs, collapsed cave systems that open into hidden lagoons inside the islands, and the entrances are low tunnels that only a kayak can pass, and only at the right tide. You go in with a paddler who knows which openings are passable that day.

Koh Panyee is a Muslim fishing village built on stilts against a cliff, founded by Javanese fishing families in the eighteenth century. It has a mosque, a school, and a floating football pitch the village built itself after watching a World Cup and deciding the lack of flat ground was not a good enough reason not to play.

The longtail is slow and loud compared to a speedboat. It is also the boat that has worked this bay for generations, and at its pace the bay reads as a landscape rather than a series of stops.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, the longtail with a local captain, an English-speaking guide, sea kayaking with a paddler, Thai lunch and drinking water.

Eight hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Koh Tapu viewed from the beach, as the rules now require
Kayak into sea caves only passable at the right tide
Koh Panyee stilt village and its self-built floating pitch
Traditional longtail, the boat that has always worked this bay
Kayaking with a paddler who knows the day's openings

fullDescription:
Four hours with elephants that are not ridden, on a programme built around care rather than performance.

The word ethical is used loosely across Thailand, so here is what it means on this visit: no riding, no chains during the programme, no shows. The time is spent preparing food, carrying out a basic health check, feeding, and generally observing animals that are doing normal elephant things rather than routines.

The health check is the part that teaches most. You learn what to look for on an Asian elephant: the condition of the feet, which carry several tonnes and are where most captive elephants fail; the state of the skin behind the ears; how the animal holds its trunk when it is relaxed. Once you know what a healthy elephant looks like you can read any camp you pass in Thailand, which is more useful than any single visit.

Worth knowing honestly: Asian elephants in Thailand are almost entirely captive-bred or rescued from logging and trekking work. A sanctuary is a retirement arrangement, not a wild population, and the animals still depend on people for food and veterinary care. Places that promise wild behaviour are overselling.

Wear clothes you do not mind getting dirty, because you will.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers learning about Asian elephants, preparing their food, the health check, feeding and care time.

Four hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: No riding, no chains during the programme, no shows
Prepare food, feed, and carry out a basic health check
Learn what a healthy elephant looks like, and read any camp after
Rescued and retired animals, not a wild population
Wear clothes you do not mind ruining

fullDescription:
A short visit near Krabi Town spent washing rescued elephants, with their regular keepers rather than a rotating tour crew.

The shelter takes animals out of riding camps and logging work. An hour and a half is enough for the bathing session and the stories, and not enough to pretend you are doing conservation work, which is an honest framing rather than a shortcoming.

No riding, no chains, no performances. The elephants go into the water because they like being in the water, and you go in with them with a brush.

What makes this worth doing over a larger camp is that the keepers who work with each animal every day run the session. They know the individual histories: which camp an elephant came out of, what the injuries are, why one is nervous around certain sounds. Those stories are specific rather than a script, and they are the actual content of the visit.

An honest caveat about bathing generally: some welfare specialists argue that repeated bathing sessions with strangers are themselves a form of performance, and a few of the best-regarded sanctuaries in Thailand have stopped them for that reason. This shelter runs them. If that matters to you, a look-and-feed-only programme may suit you better, and there are ones in Krabi that do exactly that.

Shelter clothing, a locker, showers, a towel and drinking water are provided, so you can arrive in normal clothes.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. Ninety minutes, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Rescued elephants, no riding, chains or performances
Session run by the keepers who work with them daily
Each animal's rescue history, not a script
Clothing, locker, shower and towel provided
Honest note: some sanctuaries now avoid bathing sessions entirely

fullDescription:
A full day around the Hong Island group, built around a lagoon you enter through a gap in a cliff.

Koh Hong's lagoon is the reason the island is on every Krabi itinerary. It is a shallow pool of green water almost completely enclosed by limestone walls, and the only way in is a narrow passage that boats can pass at some tides and not others. Inside, the walls cut the wind and the water goes flat, which is why it photographs the way it does.

The viewpoint is a climb, and a steep one. The reward is the whole island group laid out below with the bay behind it, and it is the picture people actually keep from a Krabi trip.

Koh Lao Lading is the other stop worth naming: a small island with a single overhanging cliff leaning out above a curve of sand. After James Bond Island it is the most photographed rock formation in the bay, and it is far quieter.

Snorkelling is over sheltered reef. This island group sits inside the bay rather than out towards Phi Phi, so the water stays workable on days when the open crossings are rough, which makes it a more reliable booking in the green season from May to October.

Speedboat transfers between the islands keep a seven-hour day from becoming a day of travelling.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, speedboat transfers, an English-speaking guide, lunch, drinking water and soft drinks, and snorkelling equipment.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Hong Lagoon, entered through a tide-dependent cliff passage
Steep climb to the 360-degree island viewpoint
Koh Lao Lading's overhanging cliff, far quieter than Koh Tapu
Sheltered water that holds up when open crossings are rough
Speedboat between islands, so the day is not spent travelling
